classification.difficultyReason: Interpret three reference angles and use quadrant signs to express unit-circle coordinates in terms of sine and cosine.

content.prompt:
The points $P,Q,R$ are on the unit circle. $O$ is the origin.
Find the coordinates of $P,Q,R$.
Leave your answer in terms of $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute reference angle.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5, unit-circle diagram beneath the instruction
spec.description: Unshaded unit circle with positive x- and y-axis arrows. Three labelled circumference points and radii. Separate arcs show 80 degrees above the positive x-axis, 55 degrees below the positive x-axis and 20 degrees below the negative x-axis. The origin label is omitted under the house graph convention; the stem retains O as the origin.
spec.mathematics: Q lies at 80 degrees, P at 305 degrees and R at 200 degrees on a circle of radius 1 centred at the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: All points, radii, angle measures and axis labels are permanent givens. Coordinate answers are hidden.

answer.worked: On the unit circle, coordinates are $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ with signs determined by the quadrant. $P$ is in quadrant IV with reference angle $55^{\circ}$, so $P=(\cos55^{\circ},-\sin55^{\circ})$.
$Q$ is in quadrant I with reference angle $80^{\circ}$. Both coordinates are positive, so $Q=(\cos80^{\circ},\sin80^{\circ})$.
$R$ is in quadrant III with reference angle $20^{\circ}$. Both coordinates are negative, so $R=(-\cos20^{\circ},-\sin20^{\circ})$.
